security_spec.violation_condition: QEMU's CHERI capability decode/encode logic references the old 'M-bit' field name internally (e.g., in TCG-generated bit manipulation or CSR read/write handlers) and the rename to 'P-bit' in the spec causes a mismatch where the wrong capability metadata bit position is read or written, or when the P-bit encoding rule (for non-x_perm capabilities the P-bit must always be interpreted/reported as CAP_MODE_VALUE) is not enforced
security_spec.vulnerability_pattern: m_bit|M_BIT|MODE_BIT|cheri_mode_bit|mbit|MBIT in QEMU target/riscv CHERI capability format encoding/decoding or CSR handler code, which must be renamed to match spec p_bit/P-bit and must enforce the non-x_perm P-bit=CAP_MODE_VALUE masking rule
security_spec.summary: Spec PR renames M-bit to P-bit across all CHERI capability encodings (RV32/RV64) and CSR tables with no bit-position change; QEMU emulation must update internal field names, CSR handler logic, and TCG capability decode/encode to match the new P-bit nomenclature and enforce the rule that P-bit reads as CAP_MODE_VALUE for non-executable capabilities

findings.finding: No CHERI capability format encoding/decoding code exists in this QEMU tree. The upstream qemu/qemu.git repository does not implement CHERI extensions. No M-bit/P-bit references, capability decode/encode functions, or CHERI CSR handlers were found anywhere in target/riscv/. The vulnerability pattern (m_bit|M_BIT|MODE_BIT|cheri_mode_bit|mbit|MBIT) returns zero matches in capability context. The spec documents at spec_ref/riscv-cheri/ define the normative P-bit rules (e.g., sec_m_bit_hybrid_rule at riscv-hybrid-integration.adoc:120-129 requiring non-x_perm capabilities to always report CAP_MODE_VALUE), but there is no corresponding emulation code to audit.
findings.snippet: N/A — code locations do not exist

spec_citations.excerpt: For capabilities that do not grant x_perm, the M-bit must always be interpreted and reported as CAP_MODE_VALUE representing Capability Mode.

When Zyhybrid is supported, capabilities include an m_bit (bit 52). If the capability does not grant x_perm or Zyhybrid is not supported, the m_bit is always reserved and so must be zero in valid capabilities.
